name: update_field_via_table_call
description: Calls a function taken from a table inside the structure passed as the first argument, then writes the second argument into the structure that call returns at a fixed field offset. The pseudo-code shows only that call and the store.

name: chain_two_calls_conditionally
description: Calls one routine with the last two arguments, and if it returns a non-zero value calls a second routine with the first two arguments and that value. If the second call fails it makes a follow-up call and returns zero; otherwise it returns the first value.

name: read_and_copy_icon_record
description: Reads a record through a helper, then copies a 44-byte block and several fields from a stack buffer into the record and links it into a parent record when one is set. It returns the record, or zero when the read fails.

name: copy_record_fields_and_link
description: Copies a 44-byte block and several fields from a source area into the record named by the register inputs, then links the record into the parent it points to when one exists. It has no return value beyond the copy.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Library routine that does nothing and returns zero. It is called from two places and performs no memory or library operations.

name: pack_record_and_forward
description: Builds a small two-word header on the stack, copies a 44-byte block and several fields from the record given as the third argument into the stack buffer, then passes that buffer to one other routine. It returns nothing.

name: read_info_icon_file
description: Reads an icon (.info) file: it builds the file name from a text reference, opens it through a helper, reads a 78-byte header and checks its magic number and version, then reads the optional image and tool-data sections the header describes. It returns one on success and zero on failure, closing the handle either way.

name: read_info_icon_sections
description: Continues reading an icon file after its header is in place: it checks the magic number and version, reads the stored fields into the record, and allocates the optional image and tool-data blocks, copying each in from the file. It returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: read_icon_optional_blocks
description: Reads two stored fields into the icon record, then reads an optional block list and a further optional block, allocating memory for each and copying the data in from the file. It returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: read_icon_pointer_list
description: Fills a list of 4-byte entries from the file in a loop until the remaining byte count drops to four, then reads an optional extra value into the record. It returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: return_zero_after_call
description: Calls one other routine, discards its result, and returns zero. The pseudo-code has no other operations.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: write_info_icon_file
description: Writes an icon (.info) file: it allocates a 260-byte work buffer, builds the file name from a text reference, opens the file, then writes the header and the optional sections the record describes. It frees the buffer and restores a saved field before returning one on success or zero on failure.

name: write_icon_record_sections
description: Writes the optional sections of an icon record to a file: it saves one stored field, clears it for one flag combination, writes a block followed by the optional image and tool-data sections, then restores the field. It returns one when every write succeeds and zero otherwise.

name: write_icon_tool_strings
description: Writes the optional string list and extra value of an icon record: each string is written as a length followed by its text, then an optional trailing value is written. It restores a saved field before returning one on success or zero on failure.

name: write_remaining_string_list
description: Writes the rest of a pointer-based string list and the optional extra value of an icon record, returning one on success and zero on failure. It restores a saved field before returning.

name: write_string_pointer_list
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of pointers, writing each entry as a length followed by its text, then writes an optional extra value. It returns one when all writes succeed and zero otherwise.

name: drain_linked_list
description: Repeatedly takes the next item from a list headed at a fixed offset in the second argument and passes it to another routine, until the list is empty. It returns nothing.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: forward_with_shifted_pointer
description: Calls the same routine with the first argument unchanged and the second argument advanced by a fixed offset, then returns. It passes the call on without any other work.

name: allocate_icon_record
description: Allocates a zeroed 168-byte record, initializes one of its embedded list fields, and reads its data through a helper. It frees the record and returns zero if the first read fails; otherwise it returns the record when the second step succeeds, or zero if it does not.

name: forward_no_arg_call
description: Library routine that makes a single call to an unnamed routine and returns, with no arguments or results of its own.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Library routine that does nothing and returns zero. It is called from two places and performs no memory or library operations.

name: store_pair_next_slot
description: Decrements a 16-bit index, growing a table through a helper when the index runs out, then stores two 32-bit values from its arguments into the next slot. It returns one on success and zero if the table cannot grow.

name: decrement_counter_and_store_pair
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter, then stores two 32-bit values from its arguments into consecutive slots of a table at the counter's position, and returns one.

name: allocate_small_icon_record
description: Allocates a zeroed 94-byte record, reads its data through one helper and then a second helper, freeing the record and returning zero if either fails. Otherwise it returns the record.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: call_library_then_return_zero
description: Calls a function pointer taken from a global variable through the library base, with no arguments, then returns zero. The call's result is not used.

name: forward_with_shifted_pointer
description: Calls the same routine with the first argument unchanged and the second argument advanced by a fixed offset, then returns. It passes the call on without any other work.

name: find_tagged_value_in_list
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of pointers looking for an entry whose text matches the given key and has an equals sign at the matching position. It returns a pointer to the text just after that sign, or zero when no entry matches.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Does nothing and returns zero, with no calls or memory access.

name: scan_entry_chain_for_length
description: Scans a chain of entries using a helper that finds each next link, comparing each entry's length with a value derived from the second argument. It returns one when a matching-length entry fails its check and zero when the chain is exhausted or invalid.

name: scan_entry_chain_for_length
description: Scans a chain of entries using a helper that finds each next link, comparing each entry's length with a value derived from the second argument. It returns one when a matching-length entry fails its check and zero when the chain is exhausted.

name: find_matching_length_entry
description: Walks a chain of entries using a helper that finds each next link, comparing each entry's length with a value passed in a register. It returns one when an entry matches the length and passes a check call, and zero when the chain ends.

name: find_first_matching_length_entry
description: Searches a chain of entries from a null start: it returns zero at once when the start link is empty, and one when an entry with the expected length passes its check.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Library routine that does nothing and returns zero. It is called from two places and performs no memory or library operations.

name: build_copy_name_from_source
description: Builds the name for a copy from its source name. If the source begins with a copy prefix it takes the copy number after the prefix and writes the next number into the new name; otherwise it starts at the first copy.

name: parse_copy_number_in_name
description: Parses the copy number that follows a copy prefix in a name. If the number is valid and the text after it matches, it updates the stored name, and it makes two follow-up calls either way.

name: parse_decimal_digits_from_text
description: Reads decimal digits from a text pointer into a number, and if any digits were read and the text that follows matches a prefix, it makes two follow-up calls before returning.

name: parse_copy_number_text
description: Parses a decimal copy number from a name written in the copy-of form and checks the text that follows it. It makes two follow-up calls whether or not the match succeeds.

name: char_to_decimal_digit
description: Converts one character code to its decimal digit value, returning the value for the characters zero to nine and minus one for any other character.

name: call_library_function_no_args
description: Calls one library function through a library base pointer held in data, passing no arguments and returning nothing. The single call is its only work.

description: Allocates a cleared 96-byte record, sets a default value of ten in one of its fields and in the caller's short, then passes the record on to a helper. It returns true when the allocation succeeded and false otherwise.

name: divide_unsigned_32_by_16
description: Divides an unsigned 32-bit dividend by an unsigned divisor and returns the quotient and remainder together. It uses a bit-by-bit loop for divisors above the 16-bit range and direct 16-bit divisions for smaller ones.

name: restoring_divide_loop_16
description: Performs sixteen steps of restoring division, shifting bits from the dividend into a partial remainder and subtracting the divisor when it fits. It leaves the quotient and remainder in the registers it was given.

name: multiply_32_bit_integers
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values held in registers using 16-bit partial products, and returns the low 32 bits of the result.

name: get_string_length
description: Returns the number of characters before the zero terminator of a string. The count is held in a 16-bit counter, so it stops at the limit of that counter.

name: find_char_in_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for the first occurrence of a given character and returns a pointer to it, or null if the character is absent.

name: return_zero_stub

name: copy_c_string
description: Copies a zero-terminated string from the source pointer to the destination, including the terminator.

name: append_c_string
description: Appends a zero-terminated source string to the end of the destination string, including its terminator.

name: strings_differ_up_to_count
description: Compares up to a given number of characters of two strings and returns one if they differ, or zero if they match up to that count or the terminator is reached.

name: return_one_stub
description: Does nothing and returns one; the pseudo-code has no calls or memory access.

name: scan_string_limited_then_call
description: Walks a string for up to a given count of characters and, if it reaches the terminator, makes one follow-up call. It returns nothing.

name: forward_no_arg_call
description: Library routine that makes a single call to an unnamed routine and returns, with no arguments or results of its own.

name: copy_string_with_fixed_length
description: Copies at most a given number of characters from a source string into the destination, stopping at its terminator, then fills the rest of the space with zero bytes.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: init_self_linked_list_header
description: Initializes a list header in a memory block: it stores the block's own address plus four in the first word, clears the second word, and stores the block's address in the third word. It returns nothing.

name: conditional_library_branching
description: Returns one when the pointer argument is null. Otherwise it calls one routine and, if that succeeds, makes two further calls, the last using a value read from the pointer, and returns the result of the last call; it returns zero when the first call fails.

name: walk_entry_list_applying_action
description: Walks a linked list of entries, applying one helper to each entry and to the counted block it points to, then following the next link. It returns one when the list ends and zero if any step fails.

name: return_one_stub
description: Does nothing and returns one; the pseudo-code has no calls or memory access.

name: return_zero_stub

name: allocate_optional_node_with_field
description: Allocates a cleared 20-byte node when the flag argument is non-zero, fills one of its fields from a call that uses the other arguments, and returns the node. It returns minus one when any step fails and zero when the flag is zero.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Does nothing and returns minus one; the pseudo-code has no calls or memory access.

name: build_linked_node_list
description: Builds a linked list of 16-byte nodes, one per entry of a source description: each entry gets a cleared node, a block sized from the entry's count field, and a link to the previous node. It returns zero when there are no entries and minus one when an allocation or call fails.

name: read_entry_node_list
description: Reads node entries in a loop, allocating a cleared node for each and a block sized from the entry's count, then links them into a list. It returns the head of the list, or minus one when an allocation fails.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Does nothing and returns minus one; the pseudo-code has no calls or memory access.

name: call_raw_do_fmt
description: Calls the exec library's formatted-output routine through the library base pointer and returns nothing. The pseudo-code passes no arguments of its own.

name: store_single_byte
description: Writes one byte from a data register to the address held in an address register and returns nothing.

name: allocate_handle_store_value
description: Calls a library function through the library base; if it returns a non-zero handle, stores the caller's value in a fixed field of that handle and calls a second library function with it. It returns whether the first call produced a handle.

name: check_and_set_font_handle
description: Calls a library function through the library base; if it returns a non-zero handle, stores the argument in a fixed field of that handle and calls a second library function. It returns whether the first call produced a handle.

name: open_font_libraries_and_init
description: Opens the libraries named in its text, and on success initializes a self-linked list header inside the structure and returns it. If an open fails it releases the structure through the memory-free call and returns zero.

name: release_unused_entries_and_close
description: Walks a list of entries, removing those with no remaining users and releasing each through the segment-unload call. If the owner then has no users it closes the two libraries, frees the owner and returns its stored value; otherwise it sets a pending flag and returns zero.

name: free_owner_when_unused
description: Checks whether the structure has no remaining users; if so it closes the two libraries, frees the structure, unlinks it from its list, and returns its stored value. Otherwise it sets the pending flag and returns zero.

name: set_pending_flag_return_zero
description: Sets the high bit of a flag byte in the structure to mark it as pending and returns zero.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: clear_flag_and_increment_counter
description: Clears the high bit of a flag byte in the structure and increments a 16-bit user counter stored beside it. It returns nothing.

name: decrement_users_then_maybe_release
description: Decrements a 16-bit user counter in the structure; when the counter is still non-zero and the pending flag is set, it calls a library function and returns its result. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Does nothing and returns zero; the pseudo-code has no calls or memory access.

name: build_font_entry_list
description: Fills a buffer with font entries: it first copies the names of the fonts already held in the library's list, then, when a second flag is set, scans the FONTS directory for font files. It returns zero when everything fits, or the amount by which the buffer was too small.

name: scan_font_directory_entries
description: Scans the FONTS directory for font files and copies each matching entry's name and size fields into the caller's buffer. It returns zero when everything fits, or the shortfall otherwise.

name: copy_font_name_entries
description: Copies font name entries from a text buffer into the output buffer one at a time, and when the flag is set also scans the FONTS directory. It returns zero when all entries fit, or the shortfall otherwise.

name: scan_fonts_directory
description: Scans the FONTS: directory for .font files and, for each one, reads its name and size into an entry in the output buffer. It returns zero when the entries fit, or the amount by which the buffer was too small.

name: copy_font_entries_from_list
description: Adds font entries to the output buffer by copying each source record's name and fields, then runs the closing calls. It returns zero when everything fits, or the shortfall otherwise.

name: copy_name_add_font_entries
description: Copies a font name from a text pointer into the work buffer, then adds entries for each matching font, scanning the FONTS directory for more when the flag is set. It returns the shortfall when the output buffer runs out.

name: add_verified_font_entries
description: Adds font entries whose header reads back as the expected signature value, copying names and size fields into the output buffer, then continues the directory scan. It returns zero when everything fits, or the shortfall otherwise.

name: finish_font_scan_return_shortfall
description: Closes the open handles used by the font scan and returns the shortfall: zero when all entries fit into the buffer, and the number of missing bytes otherwise.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Does nothing and returns zero; the pseudo-code has no calls or memory access.

name: score_font_match
description: Scores how closely a requested font matches a candidate by comparing their sizes and style bits. The score starts from the size difference and is reduced for each style bit that differs, so a higher score means a better match, and a candidate with no size gets a very low score.

name: penalize_style_bit_differences
description: Subtracts a weight from a running score for each of seven style bits that differs between the two style fields, and returns the adjusted score.

name: penalize_masked_style_differences
description: Walks the style-bit positions selected by a mask, subtracting a weight at each position where the two fields differ, and returns the adjusted score.

name: penalize_alternate_style_bits
description: Walks seven style-bit positions, subtracting a weight at each position the mask selects as different, and returns the adjusted score.

name: return_minimum_font_score
description: Returns the lowest score constant, which marks a candidate font as unusable.

name: select_best_font_candidate
description: Chooses the best matching font for a request: it copies the requested name, looks up the font-directory entry, then scores each candidate and keeps the highest-scoring one. A candidate whose type code matches is placed in the library's font list and counted, and the chosen entry is returned.

name: select_best_font_candidate
description: Chooses the best matching font for a request: it looks up the font-directory entry, scores each candidate against the requested size and style, and keeps the highest-scoring one. A candidate whose type code matches is placed in the library's font list, and the chosen entry is returned.

name: pick_font_entries_by_score
description: Repeatedly scores the entries of a font table and places the best-scoring entry with a matching type code in the font list, until no entry scores above the minimum. It then cleans up and returns the last chosen entry.

name: register_best_font_entries
description: Repeatedly picks the best-scoring font entry from a table and registers it in the system font list and the graphics font list, returning the last chosen entry once no candidate remains.

name: pick_font_entries_by_score
description: Chooses the best-scoring entry in a font table, marks it used, and repeats until no entry scores above the minimum. It then returns the last chosen entry.

name: pick_or_close_font_entries
description: Repeatedly picks the best-scoring entry in a font table and either registers it in the font list or, when its type code does not match, closes it through the graphics close-font routine. It returns once no candidate remains.

name: dispatch_exec_alloc_mem_call
description: Forwards its arguments to the exec library's memory allocation routine through the library base pointer. The pseudo-code shows only this forwarding call and returns nothing.

name: dispatch_exec_free_mem_call
description: Forwards its arguments to the exec library's memory-free routine through the library base pointer. The pseudo-code shows only this forwarding call and returns nothing.

name: dispatch_dos_open_call

name: dispatch_dos_close_call

name: dispatch_dos_unlock_call

name: dispatch_dos_ex_next_call

name: dispatch_dos_current_dir_call
description: Forwards its arguments to the DOS library's current-directory routine through the library base pointer and returns nothing. The pseudo-code shows only this forwarding call.

name: dispatch_dos_load_seg_call
description: Forwards its arguments to the DOS library's LoadSeg routine through the library base pointer and returns nothing. The pseudo-code shows only this forwarding call.

name: dispatch_dos_unload_seg_call
description: Forwards its arguments to the DOS library's UnLoadSeg routine through the library base pointer and returns nothing. The pseudo-code shows only this forwarding call.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies a zero-terminated string from the source into the destination, including the terminator.

name: seek_string_end_then_call
description: Advances a pointer to the zero terminator of a string and makes one follow-up call with that position and the second argument. It returns nothing.

name: compare_byte_before_pointer
description: Compares the byte just before one pointer with the byte at another pointer, returning minus one when the earlier byte is smaller and one otherwise.

name: find_char_in_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for the first occurrence of a given character and returns a pointer to it, or null if the character is absent.

name: find_char_from_current_position
description: Advances from the current position in a string until it finds a preset character, returning a pointer to it, or null if the terminator comes first.

description: Scans a zero-terminated string backward from its end for a given character and returns a pointer to its last occurrence, or null if none is found.

name: scan_back_for_preset_char

description: Returns a global value with a fixed set of bit positions masked off and does nothing else.

description: Does nothing and returns; the listed hardware interrupt request register is referenced in the facts but not in the pseudo-code.

name: store_stack_word_to_global
description: Copies a 16-bit value from the top of the stack into a global variable and returns. The listed facts also note a touch of the interrupt request hardware register.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Does nothing and returns zero, with no calls or memory access in the pseudo-code.

name: set_flag_bit_in_struct
description: Sets bit one in a flag byte at a fixed offset of the structure passed in an address register, then returns.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns; the listed custom-chip register is referenced in the facts but not in the pseudo-code.

name: store_register_to_global
description: Copies the value from a data register into a global variable and returns. The listed facts also note a touch of a CIA port register.

name: copy_global_then_indirect_call
description: Copies a global value into another global and then makes an indirect call through an unresolved pointer. It returns nothing; the listed facts note a copper pointer register.

name: copy_byte_to_fixed_slot
description: Copies one byte from a structure, at a fixed offset, into memory at a fixed offset from a base register, then returns.

name: check_display_mode_flag
description: Returns four when a global mode value equals one of two fixed mode codes, and one otherwise.

name: initialize_sentinel_list_head
description: Writes a sentinel value into a new entry and points three list-head fields in two structures at that entry, then clears a word field. It returns nothing.

name: copy_nested_pointers
description: Copies a 32-bit value from the entry referenced by a source structure's first and second pointer fields into the destination structure, only when those pointers are non-zero.

name: nonzero_to_minus_one
description: Returns minus one when the input register is non-zero and zero when it is zero.

name: rotate_and_compare_status_byte
description: Rotates an input byte and compares it with a stored status byte, either updating the status or setting up a stack entry. It returns the byte; the listed facts also show a read of the video position hardware register.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: update_interrupt_enable_word
description: Stores a 16-bit value from the stack into a global when the first argument's low byte is non-zero, and otherwise leaves the global unchanged, returning a pair of values. The listed facts show it touches the interrupt enable register.

name: compute_scaled_table_value
description: Combines three entries of a global table with constant multipliers and a divisor, and stores the result in a field of a structure at a fixed offset.

name: set_disk_status_from_mask
description: Tests one bit of a global mask, chosen by a byte in a structure, and records a status code in the structure from the result. When the bit is set it also calls a routine that updates a message containing the text Disk, and it returns the status code.

name: negate_short_toggle_bit
description: Negates a 16-bit field in one structure, toggles the high bit of a byte in another structure, and returns minus one when that bit was clear before the toggle, otherwise zero.

name: set_field_from_bit_test
description: Tests a bit of a global mask, selected by a byte in another structure, and stores all ones or zero in a longword field of a structure. The listed facts give no caller.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: consume_bit_and_signal_event
description: Clears one bit in a global byte, with the bit chosen by a byte in a structure. If the bit was set it marks a flag in the structure, updates a counter and calls one routine, then clears the flag and increments the counter. It returns nothing.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns; the pseudo-code is a bare return with no calls or memory access.

name: clear_field_and_save_register
description: Stores a zero into a field of a structure and saves a register value into a global variable. It returns nothing.

name: compare_saved_value_then_dispatch
description: Compares an input register with a saved global value and, when they differ, makes an indirect call through a table entry. When they match it first calls a helper if a second input is non-zero, then makes the same indirect call.

name: allocate_length_prefixed_string_entry
description: Copies a text string into newly allocated memory with a leading length byte when its first character is above the space code, then allocates a structure, sets its fields from a library lookup, and links it into a list. It stores the buffer address in the structure.

name: setup_whdload_device_request
description: Opens the expansion library and, when it is present, allocates a request structure, sets its flags and fields, and adds it to a system queue with a status-register call around the insertion. If the library is missing it calls a failure routine with a fixed code.

name: call_library_then_dispatch_entry
description: Calls a library function to obtain a structure, then makes an indirect call through an entry in that structure. It passes no arguments and returns nothing.

name: send_dos_packet_and_wait
description: Builds a DOS request packet, sends it to the DOS message port and waits for the reply on the task's message port, then dispatches the reply through a table entry. It opens the DOS library through the exec base.

name: finish_dos_request_and_dispatch
description: Stores a result in the request structure and sends the reply, then searches a table of codes for the one matching the request and calls the handler at that index. It returns nothing.

name: fail_dos_request_and_dispatch
description: Marks a request as failed with a minus-one result, sends the reply, then searches a table of codes for the matching entry and calls its handler.

name: complete_dos_request_with_status
description: Completes a DOS request with a status: the result depends on checks of a handle and a library function, is stored in the request, and the reply is sent before dispatching to the handler matched from the code table.
